topic.title: Generative Models of Graph Structure
topic.overview: Graph generation learns distributions over entities and their connections, often jointly with node attributes or coordinates. Autoregressive and diffusion approaches must respect that node ordering is arbitrary while producing valid topology. Related work uses generated alternatives to improve graph matching and edit-distance search.
topic.whyItMatters: Edges form a coupled structure: locally plausible decisions can produce a globally invalid or unrealistic graph. Generating multiple candidates can support molecular design and combinatorial search, but diversity is useful only when structural constraints remain satisfied.
topic.evolution: The collection includes earlier graph-based representations and scalable random graph models, then neural autoregressive and latent graph generators. Recent diffusion methods operate directly on discrete graphs or predict final topology, with newer applications generating matching proposals. This is a broad structural-modeling cluster, not a single homogeneous generation objective.
openQuestions: How can generation enforce global constraints without sacrificing useful diversity?
Which graph statistics predict downstream validity beyond average benchmark similarity?
